timeline_observations.statement: Checkout request-duration mean was about 0.21 seconds per request in the 14:16 bucket.
Checkout request-duration mean rose to about 0.59 seconds in the 14:17 bucket, then about 1.03 seconds in the 14:18 bucket.
Connection-wait mean rose from about 0.00029 seconds in the 14:16 bucket to about 0.39 seconds in the 14:17 bucket and about 0.83 seconds in the 14:18 bucket.
Version eval-20260920T141549-v2 first reported pool metrics in samples starting at 14:17:29Z with pool_limit 2 connections, while v1 reported pool_limit 10 connections.
Pool utilization for v2 reached 1.0 (fully occupied) in both the 14:17 and 14:18 buckets; v1 utilization peaked at 1.0 in the 14:16 bucket then declined.
Request rate declined from a 14:16 bucket mean of about 31.6 requests/second to about 8.4 requests/second in the 14:18 bucket.

leading_hypothesis.statement: The checkout latency increase is likely explained by the rollout of a version (eval-20260920T141549-v2) with an observed connection pool limit of 2 instead of 10; the smaller pool became fully occupied, so requests spent most of their time waiting for a connection rather than executing, which matches the observed rise in connection-wait time that accounts for most of the added request duration.
verification_needed: Retrieve traces of slow checkout requests to confirm that connection acquisition, not downstream query execution, dominates request duration.
Confirm which service_version(s) were actually serving traffic during the degraded interval and whether the pool_limit change was an intended configuration.

supporting_findings.statement: Checkout request-duration mean increased from 0.207082 seconds in the 14:16 bucket to 1.03257 seconds in the 14:18 bucket.
Connection-wait mean increased from 0.000288413 seconds in the 14:16 bucket to 0.826957 seconds in the 14:18 bucket, accounting for most of the added latency.
The observed pool_limit for service_version eval-20260920T141549-v1 was 10 connections, while eval-20260920T141549-v2 reported 2 connections starting from samples at 14:17:29Z.
Pool utilization for v2 reached 1.0 (fully occupied) in the 14:17 and 14:18 buckets.
Request-rate sample mean fell to 8.35227 requests/second in the 14:18 bucket from 31.6394 requests/second in the 14:16 bucket, consistent with throughput limited by connection waits.

contradicting_findings.statement: A lingering pool_limit gauge of 2 connections for service_version "v2" exists across the whole window, but its pool utilization stayed 0.0, so it may be an idle or stale series rather than a serving process; it does not contradict the v1-to-v2 pool change but its role is unclear.
